scope: independent root audit of representation-invariant content normalization, exact singleton scalar valuation, mandatory saturation, portfolio and integral-specialization bounds, capacity, and zero booking

mathematical_audit.normal_form: Gauss content separation, primitive polynomial gcd cancellation, and scalar gcd reduction give R=alpha A1/(beta B1) with coprime scalar and primitive-polynomial data. A constant primitive A1 is necessarily a unit up to sign.
mathematical_audit.singleton_valuation: At every genuine singleton prime where beta B1(P,E) is a p-unit, a content-degenerate residual has valuation exactly v_p(alpha). Since v_p(P)=1, a second digit occurs exactly when p divides alpha.
mathematical_audit.saturation: After the already mandatory Q, large-prime, t-avoidance, and singleton filters, the captured content is gcd(U_11,rad|alpha|). Its logarithm is at most log|alpha|.
mathematical_audit.height: A sub-beta reduced scalar numerator can capture only sub-beta singleton mass. Conversely, positive-linear captured mass forces beta-scale aggregate scalar height; discarding that content makes the claimed height representation-dependent.
mathematical_audit.portfolios: For any finite or growing portfolio, the captured union divides the radical of the scalar-numerator product and its logarithm is bounded by the sum of scalar logarithms.
mathematical_audit.integral_specialization: If the residual specializes to an integer, beta B1(P,E) must divide alpha, so a variable denominator cannot hide scalar height.
mathematical_audit.scope_warning: The theorem does not rule out a separately proved actual sub-beta scalar divisibility identity or a nonconstant multivariate primitive cancellation.
mathematical_audit.capacity: No such actual scalar identity is constructed, so beta capacity and booking remain unchanged.
